example: We had so much fun at the party that time flies when we talk.
origin: A common English saying from older writing; the idea that time passes quickly is very old

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about how fast time passes, not about being late.
The idiom does not describe a choice to waste time; it describes how time seems to pass.
The idiom has nothing to do with clocks stopping; it describes time moving quickly.

explanation: 'Time flies' describes the feeling that time passes quickly, often during enjoyable activities. Students should not take it literally, because no insects or flying objects are involved.
